conversations.prompt:
Hey I have a bash script which is supposed to read through an array of experiment files, these experiments are run by a java programm 5 times. I noticed that the script only does the first experiment in the array as you can see with these logs :

List iteration
==========================
         experiments/Read10AgentsWithAsk.xml: 1/5
         experiments/Read10AgentsWithAsk.xml: 2/5
         experiments/Read10AgentsWithAsk.xml: 3/5
         experiments/Read10AgentsWithAsk.xml: 4/5
         experiments/Read10AgentsWithAsk.xml: 5/5

The Java program that is run is pretty intensive as it runs a heavy subprocess passed as its arguments, the issue started to appear when I added the graddle line to run the java program

Here the Json he is supposed to read: 
[
    {
        "useCase": "List iteration",
        "experimentsFiles": [
            {
                "filename": "experiments/Read10AgentsWithAsk.xml",
                "experimentName": "Iteration with ask",
                "N": 10
            },
            {
                "filename": "experiments/Read50AgentsWithAsk.xml",
                "experimentName": "Iteration with ask",
                "N": 50
            },
            {
                "filename": "experiments/Read100AgentsWithAsk.xml",
                "experimentName": "Iteration with ask",
                "N": 100
            },
            {
                "filename": "experiments/Read500AgentsWithAsk.xml",
                "experimentName": "Iteration with ask",
                "N": 500
            },
            {
                "filename": "experiments/Read1000AgentsWithAsk.xml",
                "experimentName": "Iteration with ask",
                "N": 1000
            }
        ],
        "numberOfRuns": 5
    }
]

And finally here is the script : 

#!/bin/bash

set -e

METRICS_FILE=/tmp/results/results.csv
REPORT_FILE=/tmp/results.zip
HEADLESS_CONF=/opt/gama-platform/headless/configuration
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
JAVA_HOME=/opt/gama-platform/jdk

export TARGET_EQUINOX_CP=$(ls /opt/gama-platform/plugins/org.eclipse.equinox.launcher*.jar)

echo '"Experiment name","N","CPU load","Memory consumed (bytes)","Execution time (ms)"' > "$METRICS_FILE"

jq -c '.[]' ../benchmark_targets.json | while read usecase; do
    echo "$(echo $usecase | jq -r '.["useCase"]')"
    echo "=========================="
    number_of_runs=$(echo "$usecase" | jq -r '.["numberOfRuns"]')

    echo "$usecase" | jq -c '.["experimentsFiles"][]' | while read experiment; do
        experiment_file="../$(echo $experiment | jq -r '.["filename"]')"
        N=$(echo "$experiment" | jq -r '.["N"]')
        experiment_name=$(echo "$experiment" | jq -r '.["experimentName"]')

        for i in $(seq 1 $number_of_runs); do
            echo -e "\t $(echo $experiment | jq -r '.["filename"]'): $i/$number_of_runs"
            passWork=/tmp/.workspace$(sudo find /tmp -name ".workspace*" | wc -l)

            result_file=$(gradle run \
                --args="java -cp $TARGET_EQUINOX_CP -Djava.awt.headless=true org.eclipse.core.launcher.Main -configuration $HEADLESS_CONF -application msi.gama.headless.product -data $passWork $experiment_file /tmp" \
                | grep "Result File:" | cut -d':' -f2)

            echo "\"$experiment_name\",$N,$(jq -r '.["cpuLoad"]' $result_file),$(jq -r '.["totalPhysicalMemorySize"]' $result_file),$(jq -r '.["duration"]' $result_file)" >> "$METRICS_FILE"
        done
    done
done

echo "Done!"

What do you think is causing the issue?
conversations.answer: It looks like the issue you're facing could be related to the way the gradle run command is executed within the loop. The behavior you're observing, where the script only runs the first experiment in the array, might be due to how the standard output of the gradle run command is being consumed by the script.When you execute the following line to capture the result file:[CODE_BLOCK_0]It's possible that the gradle run command consumes the standard input of the loop, preventing the loop from continuing its iterations. To avoid this, you could try redirecting the standard input of the gradle run command from /dev/null:[CODE_BLOCK_1]This way, the gradle run command won't consume input from the loop, and the loop should continue iterating through the experiment files as intended.Also, make sure to update the path to the gradle command if it's not in your system's PATH, or if it's located in a specific directory.Try making this change and see if it resolves the issue where only the first experiment in the array is being processed.

code.after:
# Setup

This benchmark runs on Github Actions standard runners, as of August 2023 here are the specs.

## Software

- Gama 1.9.1
- JDK: Eclipse Temurin 17 (bundled with java)
- Ubuntu 20.04

## Hardware

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(gtools)
library(prettyunits)

metrics_report_file <- "/tmp/results/results.csv"

    )
}

base_bar_plot <- function(data, ylabel, color = "blue", present_as = NULL) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = N, y = mean)) +
    geom_col(stat="identity", position = "dodge", fill = color) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = paste(
        "min=", if (present_as == "bytes")
            pretty_bytes(min, style="6")
          else if (present_as == "percentage")
            sprintf("%0.2f%%", min * 100)
          else min, "\n",
        "max=", if (present_as == "bytes")
            pretty_bytes(max, style="6")
          else if (present_as == "percentage")
            sprintf("%0.2f%%", max * 100)
          else max, "\n",
        "σ=",formatC(`standard deviation`, format = "e", digits = 2),
        sep="")
      ),
      size      = 3.5,
      color     = "#fbf1c7",
      vjust     = 1.6
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = mixedsort(data$N)) + # Sort the x axis as it is considered a string not an int
    xlab("N: Input Size") +
    ylab(ylabel) +
    theme_minimal()
}

nb_of_executions <- data %>%
  group_by(`Experiment name`, N) %>%
  count() # Since they are all equal we will take this shortcut

nb_of_executions <- nb_of_executions[[1, "n"]]

for (experiment in unique(data$"Experiment name")) {
  experiment_data <- data %>%
    filter(data$"Experiment name" == experiment)
  cpu_load  <- aggregate(experiment_data, "CPU load")
  mem_usage <- aggregate(experiment_data, "Memory consumed (bytes)")

  plot_time <- base_bar_plot(exec_time, "Execution time (ms)", "#076678", "time") + ggtitle("Average time taken depending on input")
  plot_cpu  <- base_bar_plot(cpu_load,  "CPU load", "#d65d0e", "percentage") + ggtitle("Average CPU usage depending on input")
  plot_mem  <- base_bar_plot(mem_usage, "Memory consumed (bytes)", "#98971a", "bytes") + ggtitle("Average memory usage depending on input")

  # Save the plot as an image
  ggsave(filename = paste(experiment, "_time.png", sep=""), plot = plot_time)
  ggsave(filename = paste(experiment, "_cpu.png" , sep=""), plot = plot_cpu)
  ggsave(filename = paste(experiment, "_mem.png" , sep=""), plot = plot_mem)
}
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
for (experiment in unique(data$"Experiment name")) {
  cat(paste("##", experiment, sep = " "), "\n\n")

  cat(paste("Experiment have been run", nb_of_executions, "times for each input size", sep=" "), "\n\n")

  cat(paste("![", experiment, "](./", experiment, "_time.png){width=50%}", sep=""), "")

# Limitations

- The JMX tool launches Gama on each experiment run, meaning that the data you see includes the Gama startup.
- The benchmark launches Gama in headless mode and thus needs a [finalStep](https://gama-platform.org/wiki/HeadlessLegacy#simulation) argument, capping benchmarks at a maximum.
